newsitem.title: USA: Westmoreland says court denies injunction.
newsitem.headline: Westmoreland says court denies injunction.

text.p: Westmoreland Coal Co said a Virginia Federal District Court denied a request by the United Mine Workers of America for a preliminary injunction to make the company restart paying 1992 benefit plan beneficiary expenses.

The company said it believes the court's order, when issued, will include a directive ordering it to pay $200,000 a week as a security for ongoing 1992 UMWA benefit plan expenses until the matter is resolved.
The company also said the court permitted it to continue using its cash for expenses incurred in the ordinary course of business.

The UMWA sought an order requiring Westmoreland to temporarily restart the payments after the company stopped making them last week. The company said it did not have the cash or the income to meet the payments, which had been costing it about $200,000 a week, a company spokeswoman said earlier this week.
The 1992 plan affects about 1,200 Westmoreland retirees and their dependents, the company said.
